[![postcss-px-conversion][image-banner]][github-link] # postcss-px-conversion A PostCSS plugin that converts px to vw, vh, vmin, vmax, rem and rpx.

[![GitHub stars][github-stars-shield]][github-stars-link] [![GitHub issues][github-issues-shield]][github-issues-link] [![License][github-license-shield]][github-license-link]
Table of contents - [✨ Features](#-features) - [px to viewport units](#px-to-viewport-units) - [vw, vh, vmin, vmax, rem or rpx](#vw-vh-vmin-vmax-rem-or-rpx) - [A design width for each breakpoint](#a-design-width-for-each-breakpoint) - [A design width for each file](#a-design-width-for-each-file) - [Landscape](#landscape) - [Values that stay as they are](#values-that-stay-as-they-are) - [📦 Installation](#-installation) - [🚀 Usage](#-usage) - [Nuxt](#nuxt) - [rem to px](#rem-to-px) - [⚙️ Options](#️-options) - [🧮 How values are converted](#-how-values-are-converted) - [🤝 Feedback](#-feedback)
## ✨ Features ![px to viewport units][image-feature-viewport-units] ### px to viewport units Write the sizes from the design in px. Each value is divided by `viewportWidth` and multiplied by 100, so on a 375px design `width: 320px` becomes `width: 85.33333vw`. ```css /* Input */ .card { width: 320px; padding: 12px 24px; font-size: 16px; border: 1px solid; } /* Output */ .card { width: 85.33333vw; padding: 3.2vw 6.4vw; font-size: 4.26667vw; border: 1px solid; } ``` Values up to `minPixelValue`, which is 1 by default, keep their px, so hairline borders stay one pixel wide.
[![Back to top][back-to-top]](#readme-top)
![vw, vh, vmin, vmax, rem or rpx][image-feature-target-units] ### vw, vh, vmin, vmax, rem or rpx `viewportUnit` sets the unit to convert to, and `fontViewportUnit` sets it for properties whose name contains `font`. Viewport units scale with the design width, and so does rpx, which divides the screen into 750 parts. rem and px convert into each other through `rootValue`, which is 16 by default. ```js // 320px -> 20rem postcssPxConversion({ viewportUnit: "rem" }); // 320px -> 640rpx postcssPxConversion({ viewportUnit: "rpx" }); // 1.5rem -> 24px postcssPxConversion({ unitType: "rem", viewportUnit: "px", fontViewportUnit: "px" }); ```
[![Back to top][back-to-top]](#readme-top)
![A design width for each breakpoint][image-feature-breakpoints] ### A design width for each breakpoint `viewportWidth` can be a function. It receives the file path and the position of the declaration: its property, the selector of its rule and the at-rules around it, outermost first. Returning undefined leaves the declaration as it is. ```js postcssPxConversion({ allowMediaQuery: true, viewportWidth: (file, { atRules }) => { const desktop = atRules.some(atRule => atRule.params.includes("min-width: 768px")); return desktop ? 1440 : 375; }, }); ``` With this setting, `width: 150px` becomes `40vw` on its own and `10.41667vw` inside `@media (min-width: 768px)`.
[![Back to top][back-to-top]](#readme-top)
![A design width for each file][image-feature-per-file-width] ### A design width for each file A comment that starts with `viewport-width` sets the width for the declarations from the file it is written in, even after several files have been combined into one stylesheet. The width is the first number after the comment text and has to be greater than 0. ```css /* viewport-width: 1920 */ .header { width: 1600px; /* converted to 83.33333vw */ } ``` ```css /* viewport-width: 375 */ .header { width: 350px; /* converted to 93.33333vw */ } ``` One build can then produce stylesheets for desktop and mobile, loaded with media queries: ```html ```
[![Back to top][back-to-top]](#readme-top)
![Landscape][image-feature-landscape] ### Landscape With `enableLandscape`, the declarations that change are copied into a `@media (orientation: landscape)` block and converted with `landscapeUnit` and `landscapeViewportWidth`, which is 568 by default. ```css /* Input */ .banner { width: 71px; } /* Output */ .banner { width: 18.93333vw; } @media (orientation: landscape) { .banner { width: 12.5vw; } } ``` Rules written directly in the stylesheet or in `@layer` blocks are copied, with the rules nested in them kept in place. The block goes at the end of the stylesheet, or at the end of the `@layer` the rules came from. Rules you write in a landscape media query yourself are converted with the landscape settings when `allowMediaQuery` is on.
[![Back to top][back-to-top]](#readme-top)
![Values that stay as they are][image-feature-left-alone] ### Values that stay as they are Strings, `url()` and names that contain a number, such as `var(--space-10px)`, are never converted. Neither are at-rule params such as `@media (min-width: 768px)`, or the descriptors of `@page`, `@property` and `@font-face`. A `px-conversion-ignore-next` comment before a declaration, or a `px-conversion-ignore-prev` comment after it on the same line, keeps that declaration as it is. The comment is removed from the output. ```css .box { /* px-conversion-ignore-next */ width: 10px; height: 10px; /* px-conversion-ignore-prev */ } ``` `selectorBlacklist`, `selectorWhitelist`, `allowedProperties`, `excludedProperties`, `excludeFiles` and `includeFiles` choose which rules, properties and files are converted. Rules inside `@media` and `@container` are converted only when `allowMediaQuery` is on.
[![Back to top][back-to-top]](#readme-top)
## 📦 Installation ```bash npm install postcss postcss-px-conversion --save-dev ``` ## 🚀 Usage Add the plugin to your PostCSS configuration: ```js // postcss.config.mjs export default { plugins: { "postcss-px-conversion": { viewportWidth: 375, }, }, }; ``` The plugin can also be imported and called, or passed to PostCSS as it is: ```js // postcss.config.mjs import postcssPxConversion from "postcss-px-conversion"; export default { plugins: [postcssPxConversion({ viewportWidth: 375 })], }; ``` > [!TIP] > > Tailwind CSS 4 puts its rules in `@layer`, and the plugin converts rules there. Its breakpoints are media queries, so they are converted when `allowMediaQuery` is on. ### Nuxt `nuxt.config.ts` ```ts export default defineNuxtConfig({ postcss: { plugins: { "postcss-px-conversion": { viewportWidth: 375, unitPrecision: 10, viewportUnit: "vw", minPixelValue: 1, includeFiles: [/\/pages\//], excludeFiles: [/node_modules/, /pages\/active\/index\.vue/], }, }, }, }); ``` With this directory structure, the `index` page is converted and the `active` page is not: ``` - package.json - pages - index - index.vue - active - index.vue ``` ### rem to px Sizes in rem follow the font size of the page's `` element. A UI that renders inside pages you do not control, such as a browser extension's content script UI in a shadow root, can convert rem to px to keep the same size everywhere: ```js // postcss.config.mjs import postcssPxConversion from "postcss-px-conversion"; export default { plugins: [ postcssPxConversion({ unitType: "rem", viewportUnit: "px", fontViewportUnit: "px", minPixelValue: 0, allowMediaQuery: true, }), ], }; ``` `minPixelValue: 0` converts small values such as `0.25rem`, and `allowMediaQuery: true` converts rules inside media queries too, such as Tailwind CSS breakpoints.
[![Back to top][back-to-top]](#readme-top)
## ⚙️ Options | Option | Default | Description | | ------------------------ | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `unitType` | `"px"` | The unit to convert from. `viewportWidth` and `landscapeViewportWidth` are measured in it. | | `viewportWidth` | `375` | The width of the design, or a function that returns it for a file and position. Viewport units and rpx use it. | | `rootValue` | `16` | How many px one rem is, used to convert rem to px and px to rem. | | `unitPrecision` | `5` | The number of decimal places in converted values. | | `allowedProperties` | `["*"]` | Properties to convert. `*` matches all, `*name*`, `name*` and `*name` match parts of a property, and a leading `!` excludes it. | | `excludedProperties` | `[]` | Properties never to convert, written like `allowedProperties` without `!`. | | `viewportUnit` | `"vw"` | The unit to convert to. | | `fontViewportUnit` | `"vw"` | The unit to convert properties whose name contains `font` to. | | `selectorBlacklist` | `[]` | Rules whose selector contains one of these strings or matches one of these regular expressions are left alone, together with the rules nested in them. | | `selectorWhitelist` | `[]` | When not empty, only rules whose own selector, or the selector of a rule around them, matches an entry are converted. | | `minPixelValue` | `1` | Values up to this number, in `unitType`, are not converted. | | `allowMediaQuery` | `false` | Convert rules inside `@media` and `@container`. | | `replaceRules` | `true` | Replace values in place. When false, the converted declaration is added after the original one. | | `excludeFiles` | `[]` | Files to leave alone, matched by path with strings or regular expressions. | | `includeFiles` | `[]` | When not empty, only files whose path matches are converted. | | `enableLandscape` | `false` | Add a `@media (orientation: landscape)` block with the values converted by `landscapeViewportWidth`. | | `landscapeUnit` | `"vw"` | The unit to convert to in landscape. | | `landscapeViewportWidth` | `568` | The width of the design in landscape, or a function like `viewportWidth`. | | `enablePerFileConfig` | `true` | Read a width for each file from a comment. | | `viewportWidthComment` | `"viewport-width"` | The text a per-file width comment starts with. | An option set to undefined keeps its default. Invalid options throw an error when the plugin is created, and so does a width function that returns 0 or less. Types are available on the default export, for example `postcssPxConversion.Options` and `postcssPxConversion.ConversionContext`.
[![Back to top][back-to-top]](#readme-top)
## 🧮 How values are converted | Target | Formula | Example, on a 375px design | | ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------- | | `vw`, `vh`, `vmin`, `vmax` and other units | `value / viewportWidth * 100` | `320px` becomes `85.33333vw` | | `rpx` | `value / viewportWidth * 750` | `320px` becomes `640rpx` | | `rem`, from `unitType` `px` | `value / rootValue` | `320px` becomes `20rem` | | `px`, from `unitType` `rem` | `value * rootValue` | `1.5rem` becomes `24px` | Other conversions to px or rem are not supported, because their size in px is unknown. An unsupported pair, or the same unit on both sides, throws an error when the plugin is created. Results round half up to `unitPrecision` decimal places, and a result of 0 is written as `0`. The plugin converts numbers in declaration values of style rules, keyframes and `@position-try`.
[![Back to top][back-to-top]](#readme-top)
